key_insight: Weld strength in FFF-printed thermoplastics depends on coupled processing, material, and printed-structure effects—not simply higher welding energy.
engineering_relevance: Reliable welding could enable thermoplastic assemblies larger than a printer’s build volume while maintaining joint integrity.
method: Critically review friction stir, friction stir spot, rotary friction, ultrasonic, laser, and microwave-assisted welding.
Examine joining mechanisms, process parameters, printed structures, and joint configurations.
Relate consolidation, defects, and thermal damage to mechanical performance and failure.
evidence_signal: The reviewed evidence links joint quality to interacting welding and printing variables, but heterogeneous materials, geometries, and tests limit direct technique comparisons.
watch_item: Evidence for microwave-assisted welding of separately printed components remains limited, so its reliability is not yet established.
paper_title: Welding of thermoplastics printed by fused filament fabrication: A critical review of joining mechanisms and relationships between processing, structure, and properties
